The value should be converted using `TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.toNanos(maxTaskProcessingQuantumMs)` before assignment to `this.maxTaskProcessingQuantumNs`.

The new constant `DEFAULT_MAX_TASK_PROCESSING_QUANTUM_NS` is calculated using `TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.toNanos`, but the value is set to a default of 100 milliseconds in nanoseconds. This might be confusing for users who expect the unit to match the name or the parameter names. Consider renaming the constant to reflect that it's in nanoseconds, e.g., `DEFAULT_MAX_TASK_PROCESSING_QUANTUM_NANOS`.

review_comment:
Yeah, in CFS this should be the target latency within a process should get its guaranteed fair schedule/chance to run IIRC.
And here, have a similarish meaning i.e. I/O will get its chance to run after this, although with a delay (our tasks are not preemptive).

TBH what CFS does is to update via a timer (the OS tick rate) the virtual time of the task running on CPU, guaranteed a min granularity time to run on the CPU or eventually perform a different decision if there are more.
